title: Lethe: Layer- and Time-Adaptive KV Cache Pruning for Reasoning-Intensive LLM Serving
one_line_claim: Adaptive layer-wise and temporal KV cache pruning using attention redundancy estimation and recency-aware selective retention achieves 91.7% memory reduction while maintaining quality on reasoning tasks.
method_summary: Lethe prunes KV cache entries along two dimensions: spatially, by assigning per-layer token budgets based on attention weight concentration (Hoyer sparsity metric with threshold-based segmentation), and temporally, by ranking tokens via a decay-weighted historical attention score and evicting below dynamic thresholds during generation, except for sink and recent tokens.

key_findings.finding: 91.7% reduction in KV cache memory usage compared to full caching.
key_findings.quote: 91.7% reduction in KV cache memory usage compared to full caching.

key_findings.finding: Throughput increases up to 2.56x on reasoning-intensive benchmarks.
Layer-wise sparsity allocation outperforms uniform pruning by assigning token pruning budgets based on attention redundancy per layer.
key_findings.quote: layerwise sparsity-aware allocation, assigning token pruning budgets to each transformer layer based on estimated attention redundancy

relation_to_herald.shared: Both target KV-cache compression in long-context LLM generation, both aim to maintain generation quality while reducing memory/latency, and both are evaluated on reasoning-heavy tasks with modern reasoning-oriented models.
differs_on: Lethe is a static pruning strategy based on attention redundancy heuristics; HERALD is a learned predictor that forecasts catastrophic failures from logit time-series before they happen.
Lethe directly prunes tokens to reduce memory; HERALD predicts when compression will fail and enables external intervention (decompression, rollback, or fallback).
Lethe operates at inference time on every token; HERALD operates as an offline-trained classifier that runs alongside generation.
